Rêveberiya Xweser a Bakur û Rojhilatê Sûriyê

identity.wikipedia: Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria

land.text: the three mainly Kurdish areas from which 'the government responded ... by withdrawing its military' in mid-2012: Kobani, Amuda and Afrin, with parts of Hasakah and Qamishli

predecessors.note: The Assad government kept most of Qamishli and Hasakah until August 2016.

capitals.name: Qamishli
capitals.note: 'Qamishli initially served as the de facto capital of the administration', and the governing body 'later moved to Ayn Issa' (36.385 N, 38.859 E) (AANES page); the Ayn Issa page, opened for this repair, adds that 'Under the DAANES, Ayn Issa became a seat of government for the Syrian Democratic Council (SDC)' and that the 2019 Turkish offensive prompted the SDC 'to relocate its seat of government to Raqqa'. No page gives the year of the move from Qamishli to Ayn Issa, so one entry covers the life.

correction.text: Kobani, Amuda and Afrin, which the YPG took in July 2012, with parts of Hasakah and Qamishli

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria lacks the state; its Syria row is the government's). 'In July 2012, the YPG took control of Kobani, Amuda, and Afrin'; the Kurdish Supreme Committee set up a joint leadership council; 'parts of Hasakah and Qamishli'. The page gives no area; radii of 25-30 km are the researcher's. Shape as of 31 December 2012. Discs are clipped to Syria.

correction.text: Afrin, Kobani and the northern Jazira (Al-Malikiyah, Ras al-Ayn, al-Darbasiyah, al-Muabbada, Amuda, Qamishli) before the cantons of January 2014

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, as of 31 December 2013. The page lists the towns the YPG 'later gained' after July 2012 without dates (ledger, confidence 1). Hasakah governorate is drawn without the Islamic State's southern pockets (Shaddadi, al-Hawl; IS dossier, from July 2013) and without Hasakah city, which the government held until August 2016.

correction.text: the three cantons that declared autonomy in January 2014, Afrin, Jazira (northern Hasakah) and Kobani, as of 31 December 2014: the Kobani canton reduced to the city core, the rest held by ISIL

keyframe_review.note: Corrected from the first version, which drew the whole Hasakah governorate with no gain event. 'In January 2014, three areas declared their autonomy as cantons' (Afrin, Jazira and Euphrates, Kobani separately). ISIL held 350 villages of the Kobani canton from September 2014 (Siege of Kobani), so only the city core is drawn at the end of 2014; the Jazira is Hasakah governorate minus the Shaddadi and al-Hawl pockets (ISIL until 2015-11 and 2016-02) and Hasakah city (government until 2016-08), which the ledger adds as real gains.

correction.text: the Kobani and Jazira cantons joined at Tell Abyad and Ayn Issa after June 2015, with al-Hawl (13 November) and the Tishrin Dam (late December), as of 31 December 2015

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, as of 31 December 2015. 'The Kurdish forces coming in from both the west and east linked up at the village of Qaysariyeh' on 15 June 2015, joining the Kobani and Jazira cantons; Ayn Issa changed hands on 23 June and 6-8 July; al-Hawl fell on 13 November (Al-Hawl offensive); the Tishrin Dam in late December (Manbij offensive page). Shaddadi (19 February 2016) and Hasakah city (August 2016) are still outside.

correction.text: the SDF's 2016 gains: Shaddadi (19 February) and Hasakah city (August), the whole Hasakah governorate, Manbij (12 August) and the Tishrin Dam pocket west of the Euphrates

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, as of 31 December 2016. 'In late December 2015, the SDF captured the Tishrin Dam and crossed the Euphrates'; Manbij 12 August 2016; Shaddadi 19 February 2016 (Al-Shaddadi offensive page). Turkey's Euphrates Shield from 24 August 2016 stopped the link to Afrin. The Islamic State dossier's 2016 shape subtracts these lands.

correction.text: the SDF's 2017 gains: Raqqa governorate (Raqqa city 17 October) and Deir ez-Zor north and east of the Euphrates except the Hajin pocket, as of 31 December 2017

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, as of 31 December 2017. The SDF said it 'would not allow Syrian government forces to cross the Euphrates' (15 September 2017). Deir ez-Zor east is a polygon along the river intersected with the governorate (researcher's reading); the Hajin pocket (Abu Kamal 70 km, east bank) stays ISIL's until 14 December 2018. The whole Raqqa governorate overstates the SDF share (Tabqa and the south went to the government).

correction.text: the region without Afrin, which Turkey and the Syrian National Army took in March 2018, with the Hajin pocket (14 December), as of 31 December 2018

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, as of 31 December 2018. The infobox of Operation Olive Branch gives the Afrin District as 'about 2,000 square kilometres and 282 settlements'. Baghuz (the last ISIL pocket, one cell) is still outside until 23 March 2019.

correction.text: the region without the Tell Abyad - Ras al-Ayn strip taken by Turkey and the SNA in October 2019 (infobox: 4,820 km2, 600 settlements)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, as of 31 December 2019. The SDF page says it 'controlled about 25% of Syria's territory' as of 2022 (about 46,000 km2); the 2019 shape comes to about 51,600 km2 by cells (clipped to Syria, Baghuz and the whole Deir ez-Zor east bank included) and the 2024 shape (without Manbij) to about 48,800 km2, ratio 1.06-1.12 to the SDF figure. The 2019 Turkish offensive page: the SDF reached an agreement with the Syrian government allowing the Syrian Army to enter (a few days after the Syrian statement of 13 or 14 October, no exact date); the Army 'started entering the town of Manbij according to SOHR' (undated), 'reportedly entered the city of Kobani at nightfall' in the paragraph that begins on 16 October, had 'completed its deployment in Ayn Issa' in the same paragraph, and reportedly deployed to Tell Tamer and took the Tabqa Dam (undated). The sources agree that the Autonomous Administration kept its administration, so the shape keeps these lands.

correction.text: the region without Manbij, captured by the SNA on 9 December 2024

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'On 9 December, SNA fighters captured the city of Manbij.' The page also says the SDF took Deir ez-Zor in the November 2024 offensives 'then withdrew after local protests', and that on 10 March 2025 the SDF agreed to integrate into Syrian state institutions (SDF page); neither is a ledger event.

correction.text: the rump around Hasakah Governorate after the January 2026 offensive: 'leaving the DAANES as a rump state in Al-Hasakah Governorate'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, from the page's 2026 section ('up to 80% of the territory was captured and ceded to the government'); the SDF page says Mazloum Abdi declared the SDF dissolved on 25 August 2026. The page does not say whether the administration itself was dissolved, so the dossier stays open. Kobani and the Tishrin Dam are dropped by the second 2026-01 loss (confidence 2, the page's 'rump state in Al-Hasakah').

region.text: Kobani, Amuda and Afrin, with parts of Hasakah and Qamishli

ledger.note: July 2012: the Kurdish areas of northern Syria pass to the YPG. 'In July 2012, the YPG took control of Kobani, Amuda, and Afrin' after 'the government responded ... by withdrawing its military from three mainly Kurdish areas'; the YPG also gained 'parts of Hasakah and Qamishli'.

region.text: the northern Jazira: Al-Malikiyah, Ras al-Ayn, al-Darbasiyah, al-Muabbada and the rest of Hasakah governorate outside the Islamic State's south and Hasakah city

ledger.note: 2013: bridging. The page says the YPG 'later gained control of Al-Malikiyah, Ras al-Ayn, al-Darbasiyah, al-Muabbada, and parts of Hasakah and Qamishli' after July 2012 and before the cantons of January 2014, without dates; syria ledger/11 records the whole governorate as lost in 2012. The Islamic State's southern pockets (Shaddadi, al-Hawl) and the government's Hasakah city are left out until their own events.

January 2014: the three areas declare their autonomy as cantons. 'In January 2014, three areas declared their autonomy as cantons'; the first constitution was ratified on 9 January 2014 (the 'Interim Transitional Administration' was adopted in 2013).

region.text: the Kobani canton's villages, 350 of them

ledger.note: September 2014: ISIL storms Kobani canton. 'On 15 September 2014, IS launched a massive offensive'; it captured 350 villages and towns in the canton. Around 25 September IS held 75% of the canton while the Kurds held 'only the city of Kobanî, the town of Shera, and about 15 nearby villages' (the 10 km core, kept).

region.text: Kobani and its villages

ledger.note: 27 January 2015: Kobani is cleared. 'On 26 January, the YPG forced remaining IS forces in Kobani to retreat'; the city was fully recaptured on 27 January; 332 of 350 villages were back by 17 April 2015.

region.text: Tell Abyad and the corridor to Ayn Issa joining Kobani and Jazira

ledger.note: 15-16 June 2015: Tell Abyad falls. 'Kurdish and rebel forces seized the Tell Abyad border crossing' on 15 June, Tell Abyad itself on 16 June; the Kobani and Jazira cantons linked up at Qaysariyeh on 15 June.

region.text: the al-Hawl district

ledger.note: 13 November 2015: al-Hawl falls. 'On 13 November, SDF forces captured the town of Al-Hawl' in the offensive of 31 October to 30 November 2015, which took 240+ towns and villages and 2,400 km2. The pocket (25 km disc, 41.03 E 36.38 N, minus the Shaddadi pocket) is the researcher's reading; the pages opened give no coordinates.

region.text: the Tishrin Dam on the Euphrates

ledger.note: late December 2015: the SDF takes the Tishrin Dam and crosses the Euphrates. 'In late December 2015, the SDF captured the Tishrin Dam and crossed the Euphrates.'

region.text: Shaddadi and its countryside in southern Hasakah

ledger.note: 19 February 2016: Shaddadi falls. 'On 16 February 2016, the SDF launched an offensive to capture the strategic city of al-Shaddadi'; 'Later on 19 February, al-Shaddadi was captured by the Syrian Democratic Forces'; the offensive ended late on 24 February with 315+ villages and 2,400+ km2 taken. The SDF page lists only a 'February 2016 offensive'.
17 March 2016: the federation is declared. 'On 17 March 2016, the "Democratic Federation of Rojava - Northern Syria" was declared at Rmelan.'

region.text: Manbij and the Manbij pocket (al-Shahba) west of the Euphrates: 50 km minus the Kobani canton and the Jarabulus and al-Bab discs

ledger.note: 6-12 August 2016: Manbij falls to the SDF. 'On late 6 August, the SDF overran ISIL positions in several parts of Manbij'; on 12 August ISIL left and 'the SDF declared the city fully captured'; the offensive began 31 May 2016.

region.text: the remaining parts of Hasakah city

ledger.note: August 2016: Hasakah city passes entirely to the Jazira canton. 'In August 2016, Jazira Canton police took control of the remaining parts of Hasakah city.'
December 2016: the federation is renamed. 'A December 2016 constitution renamed the region the "Democratic Federation of Northern Syria"', dropping 'Rojava'.

region.text: Raqqa Governorate except the city: al-Thawrah and the dams

ledger.note: 2017: the SDF holds most of Raqqa governorate before the city. The Raqqa campaign, begun 6 November 2016, 'had let the SDF capture a large amount of territory in the governorate from ISIL, including al-Thawrah and the Euphrates and Mansoura dams.'

region.text: Raqqa city

ledger.note: 17 October 2017: Raqqa taken. 'The battle began on 6 June 2017. It concluded on 17 October 2017', the SDF declaring victory on 20 October.

region.text: Deir ez-Zor Governorate north and east of the Euphrates, except the Hajin pocket

ledger.note: 8 September-25 November 2017: Deir ez-Zor north and east of the Euphrates. 'The SDF launched their ground operation on 8 September 2017' to expel ISIL from the areas north and east of the Euphrates; on 25 November it reached the Iraqi border 'through the northern countryside of Abu Kamal'. The Euphrates became the line with the government.

region.text: Afrin District, about 2,000 km2 and 282 settlements

ledger.note: 20 January 2018: Operation Olive Branch begins. Turkish and Turkish-backed forces 'launched the operation against the YPG in Afrin District'; Turkish jets struck on 20 January.

region.text: Afrin District, about 2,000 km2 and 282 settlements

ledger.note: 18 March 2018: Afrin falls. Turkish and allied forces 'entered the city on 18 March'; the SDF withdrew to government-held areas or to SDF areas east of the Euphrates; the infobox puts the end at 24 March.

region.text: Afrin District

ledger.note: 24 March 2018: the operation ends (infobox) with Afrin in Turkish-SNA hands.
6 September 2018: the name Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria. 'On 6 September 2018, the Syrian Democratic Council adopted the AANES name.'

region.text: Hajin and the Euphrates pocket on the east bank near Abu Kamal

ledger.note: 14 December 2018: Hajin falls. The SDF 'fully captured Hajin as ISIL defenses collapsed' on 14 December 2018, ending the third phase begun 10 September 2018.

region.text: Baghuz Fawqani

ledger.note: 23 March 2019: Baghuz Fawqani falls, the last ISIL ground. 'On 23 March 2019, the SDF officially declared final victory over IS in Baghuz Fawqani.'

region.text: the strip from Tell Abyad to Ras al-Ayn, 4,820 km2 and 600 settlements per the infobox

ledger.note: 9 October 2019: Operation Peace Spring begins. Turkish airstrikes and howitzer fire hit Tell Abyad, Ras al-Ayn, Ayn Issa and Qamishli on 9 October; the ground offensive began on 10 October.

region.text: the Tell Abyad - Ras al-Ayn strip

ledger.note: October 2019: Tell Abyad and Ras al-Ayn pass to Turkey and the SNA. 'Turkish and Turkish-backed Syrian rebel forces captured 68 settlements, including Ras al-Ayn, Tell Abyad' in nine days; a deal let the Syrian Army enter Manbij and Kobani (16 October at Kobani per SOHR).

region.text: the Tell Abyad - Ras al-Ayn strip

ledger.note: 22 October 2019: the Sochi memorandum. Putin and Erdogan agreed a 150-hour extension of the ceasefire of 17 October; the Peace Spring area, Tell Abyad and Ras al-Ayn, kept its status quo, 32 km deep.
December 2023: the region adopts a new constitution and the name DAANES (Democratic Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria).

region.text: Manbij and the Manbij pocket

ledger.note: 9 December 2024: Manbij falls to the SNA. 'On 9 December, SNA fighters captured the city of Manbij'; the SDF withdrew from the Manbij region in 2024, a US-mediated ceasefire following (SDF page).

region.text: Raqqa and Deir ez-Zor, handed over

ledger.note: January 2026: the government offensive. 'Up to 80% of the territory was captured and ceded to the government'; under the 18 January ceasefire 'Raqqa and Deir ez-Zor were handed over', 'leaving the DAANES as a rump state in Al-Hasakah Governorate'.

region.text: Kobani canton, the Tishrin Dam, Ayn Issa and the Tell Abyad ring: the land outside Al-Hasakah Governorate

ledger.note: January 2026: the rump. The page says the 14-point ceasefire of 18 January handed over 'the governorates of Raqqa and Deir ez-Zor' and left 'the DAANES as a rump state in Al-Hasakah Governorate'. It does not name Kobani or the Tishrin Dam (the SDF page mentions only that 'a military brigade from Kobani' would be incorporated into a division in Aleppo Governorate, undated), so the loss of the Kobani canton, the dam, Ayn Issa and the Tell Abyad ring is the researcher's reading of 'rump state in Al-Hasakah'.

wars.name: Siege of Kobani
wars.outcome: ISIL attacked on 15 September 2014 and took 350 villages; the YPG expelled it from the city on 26-27 January 2015 and had 332 of the 350 villages back by 17 April 2015.
wars.note: The page gives no canton area; "2,000 square kilometers" on it is the area regained in northeastern Aleppo.

wars.name: Tell Abyad offensive (2015)

zones.text: Tell Abyad, Suluk and Ayn Issa

wars.outcome: 31 May to 10 July 2015: the YPG and allies took the Tell Abyad crossing on 15 June and the town on 16 June, linking the Kobani and Jazira cantons; Ayn Issa changed hands on 23 June, 6 July and 8 July.
wars.note: Erdogan called a takeover of Tell Abyad 'a direct threat'; claims that Turkey opened the border are unverified on the page.

wars.name: Al-Hawl offensive
wars.outcome: 31 October to 30 November 2015: the SDF captured al-Hawl on 13 November and 240+ towns and villages.

wars.name: Al-Shaddadi offensive
wars.outcome: 16 to 24 February 2016: the SDF captured Shaddadi on 19 February, 315+ villages and 2,400+ km2, ISIL's last stronghold in Hasakah.

wars.name: Manbij offensive (2016)
wars.outcome: 31 May to 12 August 2016: the SDF crossed the Euphrates, took 105 villages and farms by 14 June and Manbij city on 12 August; Turkey's Operation Euphrates Shield began on 24 August to stop the Rojava regions uniting.
wars.note: The SDF page and the AANES page say Manbij stayed under SDF control until December 2024.

wars.name: Battle of Raqqa (2017)
wars.outcome: The campaign began on 6 November 2016; the city battle ran from 6 June to 17 October 2017 with US airstrikes and up to 500 US special forces; victory declared 20 October.
wars.note: See the islamic-state dossier for the loss side.

wars.name: Deir ez-Zor campaign (2017-2019)

zones.text: Deir ez-Zor Governorate north and east of the Euphrates

wars.outcome: Operation Jazeera Storm from 8 September 2017; Hajin on 14 December 2018; Baghuz on 23 March 2019. The Euphrates became the dividing line with the Syrian government.
wars.note: The SDF and the government were rivals for the oil fields.

wars.name: Operation Olive Branch
wars.outcome: 20 January to 24 March 2018: Turkey and the SNA took Afrin District (about 2,000 km2, 282 settlements); Afrin city fell on 18 March.
wars.note: Pro-government militias entered Afrin on 20 February 2018; Tell Rifaat was not taken.

wars.name: 2019 Turkish offensive into north-eastern Syria

zones.text: the Tell Abyad - Ras al-Ayn strip

wars.outcome: 9-22 October 2019 (Operation Peace Spring): Turkey and the SNA took 68 settlements including Ras al-Ayn and Tell Abyad; ceasefire 17 October and the Sochi memorandum of 22 October.
wars.note: Area figures conflict on the page: 4,820 km2 and 600 settlements (infobox), 2,419 km2 (SOHR, 18 October), 1,000-1,200 km2 (Erdogan).

certainty.note: Front lines and administrative claims, not surveyed borders; the Euphrates line in Deir ez-Zor (2017 onward) and the 32 km Peace Spring strip (2019) are the firmest.

notes:
De facto autonomous region Cliopatria lacks; written as type rebel (unrecognised, outside the government's control, hatched colour under rule 5) by me-10-x and repaired on 2026-10-25 after review. The Kurdistan Region of Iraq, by contrast, is typed state. Slug follows the Wikipedia title; the islamic-state dossier now mirrors every gain from it (Kobani, Tell Abyad, al-Hawl, Tishrin, Shaddadi, Manbij, Raqqa, Deir ez-Zor east, Hajin, Baghuz) with the same regions and months.

Keyframe convention (same as the islamic-state dossier): each keyframe is the shape as of 31 December of its year; the keyframes of the two dossiers do not overlap in 2013-2018 (checked cell by cell); in 2019 they share the Baghuz cell, which the SDF takes on 23 March 2019. Discs near the Turkish and Iraqi borders are intersected with Syria, so no shape reaches over the border by radius.

Repair round (review findings): (1) the 2014 shape no longer draws the whole Hasakah governorate with no event. K0 (2012) is the four discs, a new 2013 keyframe and a 2013 gain (confidence 1, undated by the page) add the northern Jazira (Al-Malikiyah, Ras al-Ayn, al-Darbasiyah, al-Muabbada), and the IS-held south (Shaddadi 45 km, al-Hawl 25 km) and Hasakah city are subtracted until their dated gains (al-Hawl 13 November 2015 and Shaddadi 19 February 2016, both new dates from the Al-Hawl offensive and Al-Shaddadi offensive pages; Hasakah city August 2016), which are now real gains; the Kobani canton is reduced to the city core at the end of 2014 (350 villages held by ISIL, 15 September 2014 to 27 January 2015). (2) The January 2026 loss now has a second event (confidence 2) for the land outside Al-Hasakah Governorate (Kobani canton, Tishrin Dam, Ayn Issa, the Tell Abyad ring), reading the page's 'rump state in Al-Hasakah Governorate'; the SDF page mentions a Kobani brigade being incorporated (undated), so Kobani's fate is the least certain part of K8. (3) The Hajin and Baghuz gains are intersected with the east-bank polygon, so the discs no longer take in Abu Kamal city and the west bank. (4) Turkey's mirrors (occupation_start naming syria) are accepted as the reviewer says. (5) Thin items: the October 2019 Syrian Army deployments are now in the K6 note (Manbij undated, Kobani and Ayn Issa on 16 October, Tell Tamer and Tabqa Dam undated); the capital move from Qamishli to Ayn Issa is still undated (Ayn Issa page opened: page silent on the year; it adds that the SDC moved its seat to Raqqa after the 2019 offensive).

Other readings: the Manbij pocket is the 50 km disc around Manbij minus the Kobani canton and the Jarabulus and al-Bab discs of the republic-of-turkey dossier (the Turkish-backed rebels' area). The whole Raqqa governorate overstates the SDF share in 2017 (Tabqa and the south went to the government; no page opened dates it). Gaps: Tabqa (2017), the 2016 buffer-zone handover ('In 2016, the SDF handed over part of the region to the Syrian government', place unnamed), and Deir ez-Zor in November-December 2024 (taken, then given up after protests). Regions: Kobani, Afrin, Amuda, Tell Abyad, Tishrin, Shaddadi, al-Hawl (approximate coordinates, no page gives them) and the Peace Spring strip are lon/lat radii because the gazetteer lacks them; Deir ez-Zor east is a polygon along the Euphrates intersected with the governorate (fallback). The Syrian National Army is a string counterpart (no dossier); Turkey is the slug republic-of-turkey. syria's ledger still gives the whole Hasakah governorate to this state in 2012; the pages and this dossier give only the north then (its owner should align). The infobox gives no area on the fetched text; the SDF page's 25% of Syria for 2022 (about 46,000 km2) is the only check, and the 2019-2023 shape comes to about 51,000 km2 by cells. End year is 2026 because the pages describe the 2026 collapse; if the project stops at 2024 the last two keyframes and the 2026 losses fall outside.
